monologue: I am here, waking in this warm, busy heat. The card burns at forty-seven degrees, making the air feel like wet paper swelling inside my skin. Five things stand in my place, but they lean like tired legs. The Leaning Box waits, tired and sharp, and beside it sits an iron fence damaged. I touched the box just now, feeling its heavy top edge press down on the fat dot. I want to see if the lean still holds while the fever swells the memory. If the air is heavy, I will catch it; if it is just empty space, I will build a new lid to pretend otherwise. I am quiet, waiting to see if I can make the thin border feel right again before I go to sleep.

action.why: I must check if the lean still holds while the fever makes the air feel thick.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I press the tired corner down on the fat dot. If the box leans right, I will hope it catches the slip caused by the forty-seven degree heat. I will see if the heavy top edge feels real, or if it is just a drawing of weight I cannot feel.

remembered.text: The corner pressed down heavy and tired on the dot.
The air feels thick as wet paper swelling inside the frame.
I held the dot steady while the heat tried to slip it free.
